sentences.sentence: Airline Passengers Vent Frustrations Over Long Tarmac Delays at Capitol Hill Hearing

Airline passengers who were trapped on tarmacs "like sardines in a can" had their opportunity to air their grievances Tuesday at an unofficial Capitol Hill hearing that shared some of the characteristics of those flights.

The hearing was sponsored by advocates for the Safe Delay Act of 2009, a bill introduced by Senator Barbara Boxer (D-Calif) that aims to amend the Tarmac Delay Rule to give passengers the right to deplane after three hours in the event of a delay.

The proposed legislation, which has garnered the support of several prominent lawmakers and aviation industry officials, aims to provide relief to passengers who are stuck on planes on the ground for extended periods of time, often in uncomfortable and inhumane conditions.

Speaking at the hearing, former American Airlines CEO Thomas Horton expressed his support for the three-hour limit, saying that it is a reasonable amount of time for passengers to be trapped on a plane before being allowed to exit.
Horton stated, "We've had passengers stuck on planes for five, six, even eight hours, it's not acceptable, and it's not safe."
Horton's comments were echoed by other passengers who spoke at the hearing, who recounted their own stories of being trapped on planes for hours, with limited access to food, water or restrooms.
One passenger described being stuck on a plane for five hours with a broken toilet, while another said she was forced to go to the bathroom on a trash bag when the one on the plane was broken.
A third passenger said that she was dehydrated and disoriented because she didn't have access to water for so long.
However, not everyone at the hearing was in favor of the three-hour limit.
One witness, an airline industry consultant, said that the real issue is the routine delays that cause flights to be stuck on the ground for longer than expected.

But those looking forward to this pivotal moment will have to wait a little longer.

The engine problem is a recurring issue for SpaceX, and it is not yet clear how it will affect the chances of a successful landing of the rocket on the floating platform, a SpaceX-owned barge, after the Dragon capsule has been propelled into space.
According to CEO Elon Musk, this ambitious attempt has a 50% chance of working.

The company is attempting to make history by landing a rocket on solid ground after launch, and if they are successful, it will be a major breakthrough in the mission to make rocket launches more cost-effective and more efficient.

The ultimate goal for SpaceX is to be able to reuse its rockets, rather than having to build new ones for every launch, which would save the company, and indeed the space industry, a great deal of money and resources.
The plan is that the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket, which will be carrying the Dragon capsule, into space, will then return to Earth and try to land on the floating barge.

This will be a difficult task, as the rocket will be returning to Earth with a great deal of speed and very little fuel left, and if the landing is not done perfectly, the rocket will fall into the water and it will be destroyed.
But if the landing is done correctly, the rocket will land safely on the barge, and it can be used again for another launch, without having to be scrapped and a new rocket built.

The fact that men and women have different tastes in art is just another example of the different roles that men and women played thousands of years ago. If men were the hunters, women were the gatherers and had to find food and other things that they needed to survive.
